_note: REACHED LIVE, not through the probe: clicking Insert's Container row
creates a container and selects it, which is the real production path
into the fallback profile. The board frames the inspector alone at 300;
the app has no such view, so the measurement is taken at the shell's own
1440x900 where the panel renders 299 wide (--bk-size-inspector is 300;
the missing pixel is the frame's border, which the board does not draw).
WHAT THE BOARD WON (changed in code):
header 53h/x12 -> 48h/x16 (32:3, and 642:3251 draws the same row)
header fill: a linear-gradient between --bk-bg-card and --bk-bg-panel,
which are both #FFFFFF -- a gradient between one colour and itself.
Now the flat token both boards draw.
context row 33h/x10/gap6 -> 32h/x16/gap8 (32:7)
pills radius 6 -> --radius/sm, and the two non-scope pills filled
--bk-bg-subtle instead of transparent (32:10, 32:12). The strip is
already that colour, so nothing moved; transparent simply cannot be
read back as the value the board states.
panel edge --bk-border -> --bk-gray-100 (32:2, 642:3249)
WHAT THE CODE KEPT, and why:
FIVE header controls, not two. The founder call recorded in boards.json
stands, and the board has since been redrawn to agree: 32:2 now carries
btn/pick @136, btn/select-parent @160, btn/ai @184, btn/bind @223 and
the ... menu @257 -- the same five ProInspector ships.
The 26x26 accent-tinted icon square. The board renders the element glyph
inline in the title ('OO Section', one text node), so there is no node to
join a 26x26 box to. Founder-recorded delta, left alone.
NOT JOINED, deliberately: the 11 section rows (32:14 onward). They are the
SECTION LIST, and which sections a container shows is decided by the
profile config in code, not by this frame -- boards.json already records
the six sibling profile boards as section-order matches. Joining a row
here would be asserting the board's sample section ORDER, which is the one
thing this board is not the authority on.
2026-09-08 — RE-MEASURED after the shared section chassis was conformed to
the 807 profile family, and the element name (32:4, 14/20 in ink) joined.
31 properties -> 36. It still does NOT join the section body, and the reason
is now sharper than 'the board is not the authority on section order':
THE FOUNDER CALL IS '807 GEOMETRY, 32:2 MASTER' — recorded in Figma itself,
in the retirement note the tool returns for 159:2: 'RETIRED 2026-09-02,
superseded by 32:2 (founder call in-session: 807 geometry, 32:2 master,
retire 159:2)'. Read as two statements, which is what it is: 32:2 is the
master frame for the inspector's IDENTITY — its header, its five controls,
its element name, its strip — and the 807 family owns the BODY's geometry.
The two frames disagree about the body on every measure that matters:
property row      32:2 draws 32 tall     807:* draw 34
label column      32:2 draws 88 wide     807:* state no width at all
control           32:2 draws 172 @x112   807:* draw 160 @x120
control fill      32:2 draws bg-card     807:* draw gray/50
control edge      32:2 draws #9ca3af     807:* draw gray/100
control radius    32:2 draws 6           807:* draw 4
section header    32:2 draws 32 flat     807:* draw 20 open / 28 shut
Six boards to one, and the founder named the six. So the body rows here
(32:14 onward) are measured and left unjoined, and every one of those
properties IS joined — on inspector-profile-text, -button, -input, -flex,
-grid and -media, against the boards that won.
